annotations.title: Read a Telegram channel or group

description: ACCOUNT-LEVEL numbers for a Telegram channel, group or chat — its SUBSCRIBER / MEMBER COUNT — plus title, @username, description, invite link and linked discussion group. This is the answer to “how many subscribers does our Telegram channel have”. WHICH CHAT IS ALWAYS ASKED FOR: pass chatId (a public channel’s @username, or the numeric id) — the Bot API publishes no method that lists the chats a bot is in, so there is no default and guessing would report another channel’s numbers as this one’s; list_telegram_chats reports any chat that messaged the bot in the last 24 hours. Warning: TELEGRAM HAS NO PER-POST ANALYTICS AT ANY PERMISSION LEVEL: its Message object carries no `views` field and the Bot API has no history method, so post views and a post list are genuinely unavailable to a bot — both come back under `absent` with the reason, and neither is ever reported as zero. The bot must be a member of the chat. Read-only, 0 credits. Needs Telegram connected.

account.description: which connected account: its @handle or id from list_connector_accounts; needed only when several are connected

chatId.description: the channel’s @username or numeric chat id — required; there is no default
